# ADR-003: Synthetic data, generated by code, not sanitized real exports

## Context

This project is a public rebuild of a real internal pipeline. The real one's data
included real customer phone numbers, real staff names, and real company/brand
names woven through both the code and the data. Scrubbing that by find-and-replace
across a large, messy codebase is exactly the kind of task where one missed
occurrence causes a real leak -- not an acceptable risk for something meant to be
public.

## Decision

Nothing here is copied from the real system: no data file, no exported CSV, no
find-and-replace pass. `data_gen/` generates a fictional company's data from
scratch on every fresh clone (`python -m data_gen.bootstrap`):

- `generate_reference.py` -- a synthetic CS agent roster via `Faker('id_ID')`, and
  a "prior contact" snapshot covering a controllable fraction of customers, so
  new-vs-returning detection has something real to diff against.
- `generate_conversations.py` -- inbound/outbound message pairs across 4 fictional
  brand numbers, with a log-normal response-time distribution during office hours
  and an instant-bot-then-delayed-human pattern outside them.

The four fictional brands (`senara`, `kalvia`, `alvora`, `mira`) intentionally
preserve one real architectural nuance from the source system: one brand (`mira`)
never got migrated off an older recency-only dedup, while the rest use a
priority-rank dedup with a deterministic tie-break. Both `build_queue()` (recency)
and `build_queue_final()` (priority-rank) live in `pipeline/transform.py`, and
`build_silver_queue()` routes each brand to the right one -- a real "this looks
like it should just be one function" trap worth showing, not smoothing over.

## Consequences

The generated data is realistic enough to exercise every technique in
`pipeline/transform.py` (phone normalization, response-time calculation, new-contact
detection, both dedup strategies) but never risks reproducing anything from the
real system, because it was never derived from it. The tradeoff: this demo can't
show performance at real production data volumes -- `PIPELINE_CUSTOMERS` and
`PIPELINE_DAYS` are deliberately small defaults for a fast, zero-setup demo.
